neighbours.label: The word right before 'ground' or 'soil' (also 'deep' before wounds/tissue): "in⟦ the⟧ ground", "⟦ bare⟧ soil", "⟦ above⟧ ground" — the position where ground / soil / root is the expected next word
fire: Many solitary bees lay their eggs in small burrows in the ground.
Heavy grazing stripped the slope and left wide patches of bare soil.
The moles push up little heaps of earth from tunnels in the ground.
After the flood, nothing remained in the field but bare ground.
Tetanus bacteria multiply in deep wounds where little air can reach.
The turtle buries her eggs in a pit in the ground and leaves.
Wind soon carries away bare soil that has no plants to hold it.
Some ants raise mounds, while others live in chambers in the ground.
quiet: Many swallows lay their eggs in small nests under the eaves.
Heavy rain stripped the posters and left wide patches of bare wall.
The swifts dart out at dusk from cracks in the tower.
After the sale, nothing remained in the shop but bare shelves.
Some fish gather in deep pools where little light can reach.
The squirrel hides her nuts in a hole in the tree and leaves.
Wind soon carries away loose paper that has no weight to hold it.
Some bats roost in barns, while others live in gaps in the roof.

notes: Card: ' the' x16, ' bare', ' above', ' deep'; the pole's output promotes ' soil', ' root', ' bone', ' ground'.
